title: Same Tree
oneLinerQuestion: Check if two binary trees are structurally identical with equal node values.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Same Tree problem requires determining if two binary trees are structurally identical and have identical values at every corresponding node. This exhibits a direct recursive substructure: two trees rooted at 'p' and 'q' are identical if and only if their root values match, and their corresponding left subtrees are identical, and their corresponding right subtrees are identical. By performing a synchronized Depth-First Search (DFS) traversal on both trees concurrently, we can verify structural equivalence and value equality in linear time.

- Step 1: Base Case (Both Empty) — If both nodes are null (`p === null && q === null`), we have reached the bottom of a matching path with no structural differences, so we return `true`.

- Step 2: Base Case (Structural Asymmetry) — If one node is null and the other is not (`p === null || q === null`), the trees diverge structurally at this point, so we return `false`.

- Step 3: Node Value Comparison — If both nodes exist, we check their values: if `p.val !== q.val`, their values differ, so we return `false`.

- Step 4: Synchronized Recursive Traversal — If the current nodes are identical in presence and value, we recursively evaluate both children in lockstep: we check if the left subtrees match (`isSameTree(p.left, q.left)`) and if the right subtrees match (`isSameTree(p.right, q.right)`).

- Step 5: Logical Conjunction & Result Return — Both recursive calls must evaluate to `true` for the trees to be identical: return `isSameTree(p.left, q.left) && isSameTree(p.right, q.right)`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(min(N, M)) where N and M are the number of nodes in trees p and q, terminating early as soon as any structural or value discrepancy is found. Space Complexity: O(min(H_p, H_q)) auxiliary stack space, where H is tree height, representing the recursion stack depth (O(log N) for balanced trees, O(N) in the worst-case skewed tree).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION isSameTree(p, q):
    IF p IS NULL AND q IS NULL THEN RETURN True
    IF p IS NULL OR q IS NULL OR p.val != q.val THEN RETURN False
    RETURN isSameTree(p.left, q.left) AND isSameTree(p.right, q.right)
END FUNCTION
